verdict.reason: The README (packages/backend/README.md:119-122, echoed in packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:129) asserts that CLI sign-in returns a specific `400 Command-line sign-in requires an https server` when the deployment's origin is plain-http and non-loopback. Grepping the entire backend source (and the whole repo) for that exact string finds it only in the two doc files — it does not exist in any controller, guard, or middleware. Reading github-auth.guard.ts (the only place that throws BadRequestException, line 178) shows its one 400 is for a cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site check with an unrelated message ('Start the login from Wafflebase itself...'). cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts contains no scheme/loopback check at all — it always renders the 200 confirmation page or advances via a signed cookie token, never returning a 400 for scheme reasons. oauth-state.ts's `useSecureCookies()` (lines 190-207) merely decides whether cookies get `Secure`/`__Host-` based on the callback URL's scheme; it has no loopback-awareness and produces no error response, silently affecting whether the cookie round-trips rather than throwing. So the documented request/response behavior (a specific 400 keyed to scheme-and-loopback) is not implemented anywhere in the code the README describes — a real, user-facing documentation/code contradiction, which is squarely in the Docs lane ('Documentation contradicted by this PR's own code').

verdict.reason: Verified against the backend auth code. self-hosting.md (lines 128-131) claims CLI sign-in answers "400 Command-line sign-in requires an https server" on a plain-http, non-localhost deployment, and (lines 137-139) claims NODE_ENV=production with a non-loopback http:// callback URL "logs a warning at the first login". Neither exists: isSecureCookie() in packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:184-195 silently derives the Secure/__Host- decision from COOKIE_SECURE / GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL scheme / NODE_ENV with no logging at all. auth.controller.ts's CLI callback path (lines 108-223) only throws BadRequestException for 'Invalid CLI port', a missing PKCE challenge, or an expired/invalid CLI state — none gated on scheme or loopback-ness. github-auth.guard.ts's only BadRequestException/logger.warn pair (lines 171-181) is for a cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site CLI start, unrelated to http/https. A repo-wide grep for "https server" only turns up the doc file itself and the near-identical claim in packages/backend/README.md:120; a grep for logger.warn/console.warn across packages/backend/src shows no NODE_ENV/callback-scheme warning anywhere. So the docs assert a specific error message and a specific warning log that the code never produces — a documentation-vs-code contradiction squarely in this lens's remit.

verdict.reason: packages/backend/README.md:68-70 states inline with the COOKIE_SECURE var: '`NODE_ENV=production` with a non-loopback `http://` callback URL logs a warning for that reason.' I read the full implementation of the cookie-security decision (isSecureCookie/useSecureCookies in oauth-state.ts) and every caller of it (auth.controller.ts baseCookieOptions, github-auth.guard.ts, github.strategy.ts) plus main.ts bootstrap and app.module.ts, and grepped all of packages/backend/src for '.warn(' calls. isSecureCookie() computes a boolean purely from COOKIE_SECURE/GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL/NODE_ENV and never logs; none of the 15 logger.warn/console.warn call sites in the backend relate to callback-URL scheme or NODE_ENV. There is no code path that logs a warning for a production NODE_ENV combined with a non-loopback http callback URL. The prose therefore promises behavior the code does not provide — a documentation-contradicted-by-code defect, squarely in the Docs lens's 'Documentation contradicted by this PR's own code' bullet (major). I found no guard or alternate implementation that makes this reachable/true, so refutation is not warranted.
